title: Evidence Telemetry Normalizer for Data Residency and Retention
creator: Nadia Chen
description:
Problem statement:
Redwood needs a consistent, machine-readable stream of audit evidence that ties runtime telemetry (access logs, region tags, retention config events) to normative control assertions for SOC 2 and ISO 27001. Today collectors emit heterogeneous artifacts (S3 manifests, Console events, DB retention flags) that require brittle mapping logic in downstream reports. This creates manual work during audits and makes drift detection unreliable.

Objective:
Build an Evidence Telemetry Normalizer (ETN) — a lightweight service that consumes existing collectors' output and emits normalized evidence records. Each normalized record will include: control_id, control_framework (SOC2/ISO27001), timestamp, resource_type, resource_id, region/residency_tag, retention_policy_snapshot, triggering_event, collector_source, evidence_hash, and a canonicalized artifact URL.

Scope and non-goals:
- In scope: design normalizer schema, implement adapters for Console audit events, S3 residency manifests, and DB retention-change webhook; implement an initial mapping layer for SOC2 CC6.x (access logging) and ISO 27001 A.8/A.12-related controls; store normalized evidence in the Evidence Ledger; expose query API for reporting and automated attestations.
- Out of scope: full catalog of all Maple controls, on-prem collector packaging, or long-term retention policy enforcement (these are follow-ups).

Acceptance criteria:
1) Normalizer schema documented (Confluence) and approved by Security/Compliance.
2) Adapters for 3 sources (Console events, S3 manifests, DB webhooks) ingest and output >95% valid normalized records in staging.
3) End-to-end flow for a sample SOC2 control: event -> normalized record -> Evidence Ledger entry -> Console reporting tile with control-level aggregation.
4) Regression tests and CI against sample datasets.
5) Runbook for triage when a normalized record cannot be mapped (error codes, remediation playbook).

Success metrics (first 90 days):
- Audit preparation time reduced by 50% for controls covered by ETN.
- Number of manual evidence lookups per audit reduced from median 12 to <=3.
- Automated attestations triggered for at least 2 SOC2 controls.

Implementation plan (high-level):
- Week 1-2: Schema design workshop with Security and Eng; finalize canonical fields and error taxonomy.
- Week 3-4: Build adapter framework and Console events adapter (ENG-4387).
- Week 5: S3 manifest adapter and DB webhook adapter (ENG-4412).
- Week 6: Integrate with Evidence Ledger and add query endpoints for Console dashboards.
- Week 7: QA, write regression suites, and prepare docs/runbook.
- Week 8: Staging rollout and demo to Compliance.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Collector schema changes cause mapping breakage. Mitigation: publish schema versioning and implement schema compatibility checks; include a dead-letter queue for unmapped records.
- Risk: Sensitive data leakage in normalized payloads. Mitigation: PII redaction rules and policy reviewed by Security; store only references to artifacts, not raw payloads.
- Risk: High volume of events inflates cost. Mitigation: sampling policy with retention of full raw artifacts for sampled windows; configurable sampling per customer tier.

Next steps:
1) Schedule schema workshop with Marcus and Priya (by 2026-03-05).
2) Create Eng tickets for each adapter (linked under dependencies).
3) Draft Confluence spec and provide to Security for pre-review.
